summary:
MISSIONCRAFT is an interactive, web-based space mission design and simulation platform that helps students and space enthusiasts experience the process of planning a space mission. Users can choose objectives such as lunar exploration, Mars exploration and asteroid observation. They can design spacecraft by selecting components like solar panels, batteries, propulsion systems, antennas and scientific instruments.

The platform allows users to choose launch vehicles, plan orbital trajectories and manage limited resources such as budget, fuel, mass and power. Every decision influences mission performance and success. Users can simulate mission stages, from launch and orbit insertion to scientific operations and data transmission. Unexpected challenges, such as power shortages and communication failures, make the experience more realistic.

MISSIONCRAFT also includes ASTRA, an AI-powered virtual mission advisor that analyses spacecraft designs, identifies problems and suggests improvements. After each mission, users receive a performance report showing efficiency, resource utilisation and mission success. By combining space science, simulation and gamification, MISSIONCRAFT encourages critical thinking, creativity and problem-solving skills.
details:
MISSIONCRAFT is an interactive web game where players design, fund and fly a complete space mission. They choose a destination (the Moon, an asteroid or Mars), build a spacecraft from instruments, antennas, solar panels, batteries and engines, then pick a launch vehicle and transfer route. Every choice affects mass, power, fuel, cost and risk. A bigger instrument adds mass, which needs more fuel, which needs a costlier rocket, which can break the budget. A live console tracks these limits as the player builds, and an advisor called ASTRA explains problems in plain language, such as an undersized battery or a spacecraft too heavy for its launcher.

Once launched, the mission plays out as an animated flight with random events like solar flares, communication blackouts and engine faults. Whether each event causes damage depends on the player's design, such as power margins, fuel reserves and redundant systems. Each mission ends with a score out of 100 and a 1 to 3 star rating based on science return, budget efficiency, safety and resource balance. The game turns the abstract trade-offs of mission planning into hands-on experience, so students can learn by trying, failing and improving their designs.
